summary: Yardbarker NFL writers name the hottest seat on each NFC team heading into the late 2023 season. Most picks are players (quarterbacks, receivers, a cornerback, a running back), with a few head coaches, a defensive coordinator, a GM and an owner. The intro says the most scorching seats belong to two NFC South head coaches, one NFC North coach and, surprisingly, one NFC West coach.
one_line: Yardbarker writers pick the hottest seat on every NFC team in 2023, from Trevon Diggs and Daniel Jones to coaches Dennis Allen and Todd Bowles.
key_facts: Trevon Diggs of the Dallas Cowboys suffered a season-ending ACL injury in September; replacement DaRon Bland has an NFL-record five pick-sixes.
Daniel Jones of the New York Giants is out for the season with an ACL injury, and New York can get out of his $160M contract in 2025.
Philadelphia Eagles receiver Quez Watkins has only four catches for 21 yards and missed five games with a hamstring injury.
Washington Commanders owner Josh Harris is in his first season of ownership with the team at 4-8; he previously owned the Philadelphia 76ers.
Arizona Cardinals quarterback Kyler Murray has five more games to prove himself to a new front office and coaching staff; Arizona holds two first-round picks.
Los Angeles Rams receiver Cooper Kupp, 30, has appeared in 16 of a possible 28 games the past two seasons and has 12 catches for 127 yards over the past five games.
San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan's job is in zero danger, but his reputation may be if he doesn't win a Super Bowl with a stacked roster.
Seahawks quarterback Geno Smith's completion percentage fell from 69.8 to 65.4 percent; Seattle could exit his contract after the season with a $17.4 million dead-cap hit, per Spotrac.
Bears coach Matt Eberflus has one division win and seven wins through his first 29 games, the fewest by a Bears head coach; the offense ranks 19th in yards and 21st in points per game.
Lions defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn's unit ranks 24th in points against (23.5), and opponents average 29 points per game since Week 7.
Vikings running back Alexander Mattison has zero rushing TDs and averages 3.8 yards per carry, ranking 22nd among qualified backs.
Saints coach Dennis Allen has a 20-44 record as head coach of the Raiders and Saints; New Orleans is 5-6 against the league's easiest schedule.
Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles has Tampa Bay at 4-7, 1-6 in the past seven games, with a defense allowing 363.7 YPG (27th).
Panthers GM Scott Fitterer is named the hot seat instead of owner David Tepper, who won't fire himself.
